caption:
Women in India Inc leadership went from 20% to 16.7%. That is a reversal, not a plateau.

The pipeline explanation is the comfortable one. It is also incomplete. Talk to qualified women in Indian corporate life and you hear the same three things: the idea lands only when a man repeats it, the sentence gets finished by someone else, and the room reads them as capable but not senior.

That is a visibility problem sitting on top of a promotion problem. Competence was never the issue.

In command, authority is carried before it is spoken. Bearing — how you occupy the chair, where your eyes go, what your hands are not doing. Tone — flat, unhurried, no upward lilt at the end of a statement. Calculated silence — the two seconds after you are interrupted, held, until the room returns to you.

Colonel Suhag spent 35 years learning that these are trainable. Not personality. Technique.

A number that falls can be made to rise.

topic.title: Women in India Inc leadership fell from 20% to 16.7%
topic.angle: A large slice of the qualified-but-overlooked audience is women in Indian corporate life who report exactly the brand's three symptoms — idea appropriation, being talked over, and being read as not senior enough — so the story is a visibility leak, not just a pipeline one, addressable through bearing, tone and calculated silence.
topic.why_now: The 16.7% figure landed 10–11 September 2026, is three to four days old, and is actively being debated as a reversal story rather than a steady-state statistic.

rationale: A stark two-number visual makes the reversal legible at a glance and keeps the focus on the drop rather than a stock image of a boardroom.
